# Benchmark

*Generated by `tools/benchmark.py`; do not edit by hand.* pyssms 0.1.0, Python 3.13.5, NumPy 2.5.4, Intel64 Family 6 Model 151 Stepping 5, GenuineIntel; single process, best of 3 (best-of-3 also at 10^6; absolute times vary by up to a factor of two between runs).

All four indicators (TTC, TAdv, T2, TG) per encounter.

| encounters | time-time polygon (s) | 32 combinations, vectorised (s) | polygon us/encounter |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10,000 | 0.05 | 0.03 | 5.4 |
| 100,000 | 0.56 | 0.40 | 5.6 |
| 1,000,000 | 4.34 | 4.13 | 4.3 |

The polygon column uses the 8-row form of K that applies when both rectangles move along their length (side faces parallel to the axes of the time-time plane; all encounters of this benchmark). The general 12-row form, which any convex shape and any velocity direction uses, takes:

| encounters | general 12-row form (s) | 8-row form (s) | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10,000 | 0.10 | 0.05 | 1.93 |
| 100,000 | 0.94 | 0.56 | 1.67 |
| 1,000,000 | 9.48 | 4.34 | 2.18 |

A per-encounter Python loop over the 32 combinations takes 5449 us per encounter.

Both columns use the block size that was fastest for them (polygon: the default, 500 encounters; reference: all at once, 20,000, 5,000 or 2,000). At 10^6 encounters the polygon takes 1.05 times the time of the vectorised combinations. Its value is exactness in the cases the appendix does not cover (parallel paths, standing road users, overlapping bodies) and one code path for any convex shape.
